newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS STEERING CLEAR OF RISKY OFFENSIVES.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS STEERING CLEAR OF RISKY OFFENSIVES.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Friday it wanted to break a cycle of "all-or-nothing" offensives in product markets, aiming instead to grow profits predictably from the Philips portfolio.

Addressing his first annual meeting since becoming chairman last October, Cor Boonstra told shareholders that in the past the company had proved vulnerable to market fluctuations, trade cycles and the success or failure of individual products.
"We then put all our faith in a new invention, a new product, as if it is some magic wand...We are now seeking to break out of this cycle of all-or-nothing offensives," he said.

Philips in February announced a 1996 net loss of 590 million guilders, dragged down by huge restructuring costs as it geared up to shed unprofitable and non-core businesses and address the problems at its loss-making Grundig unit in Germany.
"Now I am aware that you cannot have entrepreneurship without risk, but at this stage we do not want to put your money into projects that are beyond our scope," he told the meeting.

"This may not sound very spectacular, but that is the very point I'm making: we want more certainty, we want to become a more predictable, solidly grounded company that can offer a solid investor a solid profit," said Boonstra.

Questioned after his address about further strategy announcements, Boonstra said the company had made a start by closing down or hiving off some units and streamlining the head office operation in Eindhoven.
"At the end of this year we will be ready to face the outside world with a policy which is going to guide us for quite some time," he said.

Analysts have said they are waiting for evidence that Philips can build up profitable growth without lurching into the losses seen at the beginning of the 1990s which triggered the massive Centurion restructuring programme of former chairman Jan Timmer.

Boonstra reaffirmed the company's commitment to double-figure earnings growth in the future, saying: "We have committed ourselves to a profit growth which should be called a double-digit profit growth over the next few years." -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
